title: The Last Button

Late-afternoon light falls across folded fabrics. A stable medium two-shot keeps their faces and the jacket shoulders visible. The groom rolls one shoulder while watching the mirror. At the tailor’s request he lifts his arms slightly, then lowers them as he explains. The tailor checks the shoulder seam, makes a small fabric adjustment and smooths the jacket into place. The young man in an ivory wedding jacket (S1) has this delivery: A young man speaks in a soft middle register with a slightly dry edge. He is checking a physical sensation, sounding mildly uncertain and comfortable asking for help. The later reply is more definite, with natural emphasis on the area of discomfort and a relaxed falling cadence. The older man in a charcoal waistcoat (S2) has this delivery: An older man speaks in a warm low register with fine gravel. Calm attention and practiced reassurance guide compact, connected phrases. His final response begins with an easy acknowledgment and continues in a soft practical tone. Within 4.50–6.35 seconds, the young man in an ivory wedding jacket (S1) speaks with synchronized mouth movement: <d>[English] Yeah, just across the shoulders.</d> The lips relax after the phrase as the physical interaction continues. Within 6.35–8.10 seconds, the older man in a charcoal waistcoat (S2) speaks with synchronized mouth movement: <d>[English] Okay. Let me loosen that.</d> The lips relax after the phrase as the physical interaction continues.
